sections.html:
Appleton is the Outagamie County seat, a Fox River city of 75,452 people (July 2025 estimate), roughly 30 miles from Green Bay (southwest) and 100 from Milwaukee (north). Most of Appleton sits in Outagamie County, though slivers reach into Calumet and Winnebago counties. Your parcel's county decides where you record the deed and who handles delinquent tax, so confirm it at the start.

Several neighboring communities, including the Town of Grand Chute and the Village of Harrison, carry an Appleton mailing address without being inside the city. Building Inspections advises confirming a property is within city limits before buying a permit.

Owners occupy about two-thirds of Appleton homes, and the median value of an owner-occupied home is $231,400. A buyer's agent will likely start from figures like these.

Prep work can trigger a permit. Decks, remodels, pools, siding and sheds larger than 50 square feet are the likely candidates. Unsure? Call (920) 832-6411 first. The City Hall office is staffed for walk-ins from 8:00 a.m. to 9:30 a.m. on weekdays.

An owner-occupant of a single-family house may pull their own permits but follows the contractor rules. Any residential contractor you hire needs State registration, and the city suggests asking to see the number. A permit with an unfinished inspection stays open, which can bring a re-inspection fee later.

If you inherited a neglected house, know that the city can mow and clear debris after a complaint, sometimes using inspection warrants. Building Inspections also offers a free courtesy inspection that spells out what would bring a building into compliance.

Zoning sets different setbacks. The side setback is 8 feet in R-1A and 6 feet in R-1B; the rear setback is 25 feet in R-1A, R-1B, R-1C and R-2. Look these up before telling a buyer a garage or addition is possible.

sections.h2: The assessor and a sold house
sections.html:
Each fall and winter the Assessor's Office inspects homes that recently sold, so expect a letter about your sale, with online scheduling offered. The office also checks houses with building permits and scans online listings for work done without one. The assessor's number is (920) 832-5850.

Every property is revalued at least every five years, and the city tries to see each parcel inside and out about once in ten. A formal objection follows a spring sequence: notices in April, open book, then the Board of Review in late April. Ask the assessor for each year's dates and call the City Clerk's Office, (920) 832-6443, to file.

Owners are often surprised that a December bill is too late for an objection, and that paying under protest means nothing unless you filed with the Board of Review first.

Appleton offers four installments, due January 31, March 31, May 31 and July 31. Pay late and the installment plan ends, with state-required monthly interest on what is unpaid. Once the last installment passes, any balance is delinquent and goes to the county treasurer where the parcel lies.

  • Counter: City Hall, 100 N. Appleton St., open weekdays 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with a night deposit box after hours.
  • Mail: City of Appleton, P.O. Box 2519, Appleton, WI 54912-2519.
  • Online: use the parcel number to pay with a card or e-check. A vendor fee applies, and it goes to the vendor.
  • Delinquent bills: Outagamie County (920) 832-5065, Calumet County (920) 849-1457, Winnebago County (920) 232-3420.

Finance, at (920) 832-6442, can state your paid-to-date total, which the title company needs before closing. Refunds above $750, and any refund on a mailed or drop-box payment, arrive in four to six weeks.

sections.h2: Deed recording and the transfer return
sections.html:
Complete the state's Real Estate Transfer Return online at the Department of Revenue, print the receipt, and take it with the deed and fees to the Register of Deeds. A completed return and fee collection come before recording (s. 77.22(1)). Most of Appleton falls under the Outagamie County Register of Deeds. A parcel in the Calumet or Winnebago portion is recorded in that county.

Outagamie County records until 4:00 p.m. and charges $30 for a standard document. Documents also need the parcel number, a complete legal description and notarized signatures, with the drafter named and a blank 3 inch by 3 inch square at the top right.

On a one to four unit home, the seller hands the buyer a real estate condition report within 10 days of acceptance. A late report lets the buyer back out under s. 709.02. Storm damage belongs on the report, so keep insurance and repair records handy.

sections.h2: Renting the house out before the sale
sections.html:
A stay under a month is a short-term rental, and Appleton regulates it as a tourist rooming house through its Health Department. The license must be in hand before the first guest, and it comes with a pre-inspection and a yearly health inspection. Licenses run July 1 through June 30. The department's number is 920-832-6429.

A host who rents without a platform must register with the Department of Revenue and collect state and county sales tax once sales revenue hits $2,000, plus local room tax.

sections.h2: From accepted offer to closing day
sections.html: Once a buyer signs, the clock starts on the condition report. While that is underway, order the payoff from your lender, ask City Finance for the tax figure, and start the transfer return so the receipt is printed before the closing appointment. If the house has open permits, finish the inspections now, because a buyer's inspector may ask the city for the record. On closing day the deed goes to the Register of Deeds with the receipt and fee. The new owner then reaches the assessor's records through the recorded deed.

Appleton sellers have three paths. An agent listing exposes the house to the most buyers, at the cost of showings, inspection requests and the disclosure report. Selling on your own keeps the commission but puts the contract and paperwork on you. A cash buyer takes the house as is and can close faster, a fit for inherited homes, tenants or costly repairs.

All three paths need four things: the paid-to-date tax figure from Finance, the permit history from Building Inspections, the condition report and the transfer return. Collect them early and the closing date holds.

faqs.q: How quickly can an Appleton house sell?
faqs.a: That turns on your route and how quickly the title, tax figure and condition report come together. Listing adds showings and buyer financing, and the report is due within 10 days of an accepted offer.

faqs.q: Where do Appleton tax payments go?
faqs.a: City Finance Department staff collect through the final installment, July 31. Afterward, what is unpaid goes to the Outagamie, Calumet or Winnebago County treasurer, whichever covers the parcel.

faqs.q: Is an inspection required before selling in Appleton?
faqs.a: Selling does not require one. Decks, siding, remodeling and sheds over 50 square feet may need permits if you do that work first, so ask Building Inspections, (920) 832-6411.

faqs.q: What is the deed recording cost in Appleton?
faqs.a: Outagamie County's Register of Deeds charges $30 for a standard document. A Real Estate Transfer Return goes to the Department of Revenue, and any transfer fee is due when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Is a vacation rental allowed in Appleton?
faqs.a: Only with a Tourist Rooming House license from the Health Department, which requires a pre-inspection and renews every July 1. Schedule at 920-832-6429.
